summary: Arkwright is a dense economic simulation where you run parallel factories, balance worker wages against machine costs, and set your own prices while watching demand and competitors' output ripple through a shared market. It plays more like optimizing a spreadsheet than a typical Euro, with almost every turn a multi-variable calculation rather than a simple placement.
praised: Remarkably deep and internally consistent economic simulation (supply, demand, pricing, wages, tech all interact logically)
Strong sense of building and optimizing a real business over time
High replayability from variable setup and modular industries
Rewards long-term planning and efficiency tuning
criticised: Extremely steep learning curve and rulebook, even by heavy-Euro standards
Very long playtime (often exceeding the printed 4 hours with new players)
Heavy bookkeeping and fiddly tracking can feel like homework
Low direct player interaction — mostly parallel optimization rather than confrontation

interaction.kind: shared market and demand pools with indirect price competition, mostly parallel factory-building

scoring.why: the winner is whoever builds the most valuable block of their own company shares, driven by efficient production, pricing, and reinvestment rather than accumulating varied point sources
